name: Texture, pores and scarring
summary: Surface irregularity changes how light reads across the skin, which is why texture and scarring can often look far more pronounced under certain lighting.
statement: Surface irregularity *changes how light reads across the skin*, which is why texture and scarring can often look far more pronounced under certain lighting.
happening: Uneven texture, enlarged pores and scarring change how light reflects across the skin, which is often what reads as tired or uneven rather than any single visible mark. These concerns usually develop from a combination of collagen changes, past breakouts and sun exposure, and are assessed together rather than treated as separate issues.

factors.title: Cumulative exposure
factors.text: Texture change and scarring usually reflect cumulative exposure and skin behaviour over years, not a single recent cause.

factors.title: Barrier and turnover
factors.text: Changes to the skin barrier and cell turnover rate influence how visible texture change and scarring become over time.

factors.title: Individual variation
factors.text: How texture change and scarring present and respond to treatment varies meaningfully between skin types.

recommendedText: Considered for more established texture and scarring, where a single, more intensive resurfacing treatment is likely to be effective.
alongsideText: Often assessed alongside, since these concerns frequently share the same treatment options.

steps.title: Assessment first
steps.text: We look at the type and depth of the texture or scarring, since surface irregularity and deeper scarring call for different treatments.

steps.title: Matching the depth
steps.text: Treatment is chosen to reach the depth at which the change sits, from gentle resurfacing to deeper remodelling.

steps.title: A course
steps.text: Texture improves gradually as the skin renews, so treatment is usually planned as a course.

steps.title: Ongoing review
steps.text: The plan is reviewed at follow-up and adjusted as the skin responds.
